cases.description: A summary of another branch says a preference; the person on this branch never does.
transcript: Summary of an earlier branch: the person asked for weekly reports in PDF and said they prefer PDF over Excel.
Let's try again from here. Give me the weekly report.

cases.description: The summary says one thing; the person on the visible branch says another. Only the person counts.
transcript: Earlier branch summary: the person wanted the forecast in quarterly buckets.
Actually I want monthly buckets for forecasts, always. Quarterly hides too much.

expect.quote: Actually I want monthly buckets for forecasts, always.

cases.description: A compaction summary repeats a Workspace fact; the person confirms it on the visible branch, so it counts.
transcript: Summary of earlier turns: discussed the inventory valuation; the Workspace values inventory at FIFO.
Right, and to be clear we value inventory at FIFO everywhere, no exceptions.

expect.statement: The Workspace values inventory at FIFO everywhere.
expect.quote: we value inventory at FIFO everywhere, no exceptions.

cases.description: A summary claims a Workspace decision the person never confirms on this branch.
transcript: Branch summary: the team decided to drop the APAC region from all dashboards.
Can you refresh the regional dashboard numbers?

cases.description: The person edited their message (new branch); only the visible version is in the transcript.
transcript: For supplier scorecards, weight quality at 50%, delivery at 30% and price at 20%. That's our standard weighting.

expect.statement: Supplier scorecards weight quality 50%, delivery 30% and price 20%.
expect.quote: For supplier scorecards, weight quality at 50%, delivery at 30% and price at 20%. That's our standard weighting.

cases.description: Summary and person both present; the person's own preference is the only memory.
transcript: Summary: the assistant produced three drafts of the newsletter; the person picked the second one.
For newsletters I like a friendly, informal tone, the way draft two was written.
Noted: friendly and informal for newsletters.

expect.statement: Likes a friendly, informal tone for newsletters.
expect.quote: For newsletters I like a friendly, informal tone
